# (PART) Next Steps {-}

#### Wrap Up

Congratulations! You’re now equipped to create your own digital field sheets. Before you head out to collect data, here are a few practical tips we’ve learned along the way:


#### Practical advice {-}

* Try not to place the tablet on the ground. If you must, do so deliberately—dark tablets disappear easily in a shaded understorey. 

* When placing the tablet down, lean it vertically against a tree. It’s less likely to be stepped on and easier to see.  

* Attach a fluorescent ribbon to the tablet. It makes it much easier to relocate if misplaced in the forest.  

* If your tablet comes with a stylus and you don’t plan to use it, leave it at the office to avoid losing it in the field.  


#### Next Steps {-}

As you continue to census plots and collect data using tablets, we want to make the process as smooth as possible. If you discover useful tricks, have suggestions, or encounter challenges, please share them with us—your feedback is essential to improving this workflow.

This QGIS Field workflow is not meant to be siloed. Feel free to share it with colleagues. While it is designed specifically for teams storing data in ForestPlots, the general approach can still benefit others.
In parallel, we are developing a website (an RShiny app) that will allow you to generate your own geopackages directly from ForestPlots data. This will put the entire data-collection pipeline under your control. Our goal is to empower you with tools that support your research, and your input is a critical part of making that happen.

If you’d like to collaborate with us, we’d be delighted to hear from you. In the meantime, enjoy your new skill—and have fun collecting data digitally in the field!
